To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the linear and circular polarization of the atmosphere is negligible for stratospheric balloon observations and that the linear and/or circular polarization of the ground is negligible for observations from the ground at frequencies below 100 GHz.
the linear and circular polarization of the atmosphere are 10−12 K and 100  × 10−9 K for balloon borne platforms and 10−9 K and 100 × 10−6 K for ground based observations.

the polarization of the atmosphere at mid-latitudes due to Zeeman splittings of the O2 molecule is about 100 × 10−9 K for circular polarization and about 10−10 K for linear polarization at 100 GHz, making the atmosphere negligible for the CMB polarization signal from balloon borne platforms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the polarization of the atmosphere, a foreground for CMB polarization experiments.
the polarization of the atmosphere as it relates to CMB polarization observations.
the level of polarization induced in the atmosphere and its implications for the detection of the polarization signal of the cosmic microwave radiation background.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the atmospheric linear polarization is negligible for CMB polarization experiments, while the atmospheric circular polarization is potentially significant.

the atmosphere is a negligible foreground source for CMB E (or B) mode experiments from stratospheric platforms, while from the ground the atmosphere is a potential source of linear polarization foregrounds.

the atmosphere does not pose a problem for CMB polarization measurements from balloons and that from the ground it does not pose a significant foreground problem if the instrument has a linear polarization sensitivity of 10−9 K and if it is not sensitive to circularly polarized radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the atmospheric linear and elliptic polarizations are about 10 × 10-12 and 10 × 10-9 K for balloon and ground based CMB polarization experiments, respectively.
the atmosphere is an important foreground source for ground based experiments and a negligible source for balloon borne and space based experiments.

the atmosphere is a negligible source of polarized foreground for CMB polarization experiments from stratospheric platforms, and that the atmosphere is potentially an important source of polarized contamination if the experiment is from the ground.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level of atmospheric polarization is very sensitive to the magnetic field strength, which is a strong function of height.
the level of polarization due to Zeeman effect in the atmosphere is negligible for balloon borne experiments and for ground based experiments at 100 GHz and above.
for the CMB polarization experiments, the polarization of the atmosphere is a negligible source of polarized foreground, except perhaps from the ground.
